18	# Plan: Model teams with a charter, reference them from nodes, and edit them in a panel
19	
20	Concept: [Teams as Agents - Design](../../Concepts/Teams%20as%20Agents%20-%20Design.md) (why the
21	charter looks the way it does) and
22	[OKR Viewer - Product Vision](../../Concepts/OKR%20Viewer%20-%20Product%20Vision.md).
23	
24	## TL;DR
25	
26	Extend the existing `CompanyUnit` with an optional `charter` (mission, process, owns[],
27	dependsOn[]), add an optional `unitId` to nodes, and add three team Actions
28	(`editUnit`, `addUnit`, `deleteUnit`) so team edits flow through the same commit/undo/history
29	path as node edits. The web app holds `company` in state, ships it in the datasets, gains a
30	Teams list and a TeamEditor panel, swaps the node editor's owner field for a team picker, and
31	can show team names as labels in the 3D view. The service receives `company` with every chat
32	request, describes teams to the model, and validates team references. Schema changes are
33	additive (no `schemaVersion` bump). Multi-agent features are designed in the concept doc and
34	not built here.
35	
36	## Context
37	
38	`schema/src/company.schema.json` already defines `Company { name, units[], people[] }` with
39	`CompanyUnit { id, name, parent, lead? }` (`:36-65`), but nothing in `web/` or `service/` uses
40	it, and `createDocument` only carries it if passed (`schema/index.js:247`). Node `owner` is free
41	text (`schema/src/okr-node.schema.json:38-42`), so "Marketing" on `obj-2` and "Field Marketing"
42	on `kr-9` are strings with no relationship. The product wants a team to be a thing the user can
43	describe (business process, ownership domain) and that the model can be handed as context, now
44	for answering "what does this team own?" and later as an agent persona.
45	
46	`OKR_NODE_EDITOR` establishes `commit()` and history in `App.svelte`; this plan assumes it has
47	landed (or lands first) so team edits reuse it.
48	
49	## Goal
50	
51	Teams are first-class, chartered data in the document; nodes reference them; the user edits
52	them in a panel; team edits are undoable Actions; the assistant sees them on every request.
53	
54	## Decisions (locked in)
55	
56	1. **Extend `CompanyUnit`, don't add a `teams` entity.** (Interview, 2026-09-11.) A unit gains
57	   an optional `charter`. Nodes gain optional `unitId`. `owner` stays and becomes derived
58	   display text: the apply layer sets `owner = unit.name` whenever `unitId` changes and `owner`
59	   is not explicitly given. Additive; `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1.
60	2. **Charter shape** (from the concept doc): `mission` (≤ 1000 chars), `process` (≤ 4000),
61	   `owns` (≤ 50 strings of ≤ 200), `dependsOn` (≤ 50 unit ids). All optional.
62	3. **Team edits are Actions**: `editUnit { id, fields: { name?, parent?, lead?, charter? } }`
63	   with `charter` merged shallowly into the existing one; `addUnit { id, fields: { name, parent?, charter? } }`;
64	   `deleteUnit { id }`, which reparents child units to the deleted unit's parent and clears
65	   `unitId` on the nodes it owned (their `owner` text is kept). One vocabulary for the model and
66	   the UI; one undo stack; one history.
67	4. **State is document-shaped.** `App.svelte` holds `company`; undo snapshots become
68	   `{ tree, company, history }`; `applyDocumentActions({ tree, company }, actions)` dispatches
69	   node ops to `applyAction` and unit ops to a new `applyUnitAction`.
70	5. **One panel slot.** `panel = $state(null | { kind: 'node' | 'team' | 'teams', id? })` in
71	   App replaces the implicit "Detail is open iff a node is selected". Selecting a node sets
72	   `{ kind: 'node' }`; the Teams button sets `{ kind: 'teams' }`; picking a team sets
73	   `{ kind: 'team', id }`. `CHAT_CONTEXT` reads this directly.
74	6. **`company` rides in the chat request** (optional). The service validates it, describes
75	   teams to the model, and checks `unitId` / unit ids in actions against it. No new endpoint.
76	7. **Team labels in 3D are a toggle, off by default**, rendered with `three-spritetext` as a
77	   child of each node mesh. Teams are not nodes or colours in this round.
78	8. **People stay out of the editor.** `people` remains in the schema, untouched.

7	---
8	# Teams as Agents - Design
9	
10	Why teams get a charter now, and what that charter is for later. The near-term plan is
11	[TEAM_MODEL_AND_EDITOR](../Plans/development/TEAM_MODEL_AND_EDITOR.md); the far-term plan does
12	not exist yet and would be named `TEAM_AGENT_DISCUSSIONS.md`. Parent vision:
13	[OKR Viewer - Product Vision](OKR%20Viewer%20-%20Product%20Vision.md).
14	
15	## The metaphor
16	
17	A team's charter is a **job description for an agent**. If a human read only the charter, they
18	should be able to sit in a meeting and argue that team's corner: what it is for (mission), how
19	it does its work (process), what it is the owner of (ownership domain), and who it needs
20	(dependencies). Everything the OKR tree says about the team (its objectives, KRs, alignment
21	scores) is the agenda for that meeting; the charter is the person attending.
22	
23	So the charter is written *for a prompt*, in the same way every schema description is written
24	for the model (the schema plan's rule). Field descriptions say "in the team's own words", and
25	the editor shows placeholder text that reads like a persona, not like a form.
26	
27	## Charter shape
28	
29	```
30	charter: {
31	  mission:   "why the team exists, one or two sentences",
32	  process:   "the business process it runs: inputs, steps, outputs, cadence",
33	  owns:      ["systems, metrics or decisions this team is the accountable owner of", ...],
34	  dependsOn: ["unit-id", ...]   // teams whose output this team needs
35	}
36	```
37	
38	- `mission` and `process` are prose because personas are prose.
39	- `owns` is a list because ownership disputes ("who owns activation rate?") are the most
40	  interesting thing two team agents can argue about, and a list is diffable.
41	- `dependsOn` is references because reviews ("does Sales' KR depend on something Engineering has
42	  not committed to?") need to walk a graph, not parse text.
43	
44	## The four discussion modes (interview answer, 2026-09-11)
45	
46	All four were chosen. In dependency order:
47	
48	1. **Chat with one team's agent.** A tab with `mode: 'persona'`, `subject: team`. The system
49	   prompt is the coach prompt plus "You are speaking as <team>. Here is your charter. Answer as
50	   this team would, from its priorities and constraints." Cheapest; a direct extension of
51	   interview tabs.
52	2. **Agents review each other's OKRs.** Team A's persona is asked to critique Team B's subtree
53	   for alignment, measurability and unstated dependencies on A. Output is a normal reply +
54	   highlight, optionally actions. One call per review.
55	3. **Team-vs-team debate the user moderates.** N personas, one shared transcript, the user picks
56	   the topic and can interject. Because the service is stateless, the *browser* orchestrates:
57	   each turn is one `/api/chat` call with `mode: 'persona'`, the speaking team as subject, and
58	   the shared transcript as history (turns attributed by name in the content). A tab shows the
59	   transcript with speaker labels.
60	4. **Agents negotiate and propose tree edits.** Mode 3 with a closing turn: a neutral "coach"
61	   call that reads the transcript and returns `actions`. Actions go through `commit()` like
62	   everything else, so the user can undo the whole negotiation in one step.
63	
64	## Invariants the near-term plan must not break
65	
66	- **The charter is self-contained.** No field may depend on UI state or on another document.
67	  A charter pasted into a prompt with the team's subtree must be enough.
68	- **Team edits are Actions.** Modes 1 to 4 will propose charter changes; they must be undoable
69	  and land in history like node edits.
70	- **A team can be handed to the model without its people.** `people` stays optional and out of
71	  the persona; personas represent teams, not individuals.
72	- **`owner` never disagrees with `unitId`.** The apply layer derives `owner` from the unit name
73	  whenever `unitId` changes, so prompts that read `owner` and prompts that read `unitId` agree.
74	
75	## Alternatives considered
76	
77	- **Personas as a separate `agents` section in the document.** Rejected: it would drift from the
78	  team it describes. The charter *is* the persona source; a future `persona` field on the unit
79	  (tone, red lines) can be added additively if needed.
80	- **Server-side orchestration of debates** (a `/api/discuss` endpoint that loops). Rejected for
81	  now: it breaks the stateless invariant and hides turns from the user. Browser-driven turns
82	  keep each call inspectable and interruptible. Revisit if latency of N sequential calls is
83	  unacceptable.
84	- **Free-text `domain` instead of `owns[]`.** Rejected: ownership overlap detection between two
85	  teams is the first useful agent argument, and it needs discrete items.
86	
87	## Open questions for the future plan
88	
89	- Should a debate transcript be exportable into `history`? Probably as a `change` with empty
90	  actions and the transcript as `reason`, but the 4000-char `reason` cap may be too small.
91	- Does mode 3 need a "moderator" persona, or is the user enough?
92	- Rate limits: N personas × M turns per debate; a debate of four teams and six rounds is 24
93	  calls at ~3 s each.
94

1	// @okr-viewer/schema — the one authoritative description of the OKR document,
2	// shared by web/ and service/.
3	//
4	// Two layers, kept apart on purpose (see the plan's Decision 6):
5	//
6	//   validateX()          structural. Generated from JSON Schema, no opinions.
7	//   checkTreeSemantics() relational. Uniqueness, parent existence, cycles,
8	//                        exactly one root — things JSON Schema cannot express.
9	//
10	// Callers never see raw Ajv error objects; errors come back as
11	// "instancePath: message" strings that are safe to show a user.
12	
13	// Nothing here touches a Node built-in or a JSON import: the same file is
14	// bundled for the browser by Vite and loaded directly by the service. The
15	// package version and the tool schema arrive as generated ESM (dist/meta.js)
16	// rather than a fs read or an import attribute, which only Node understands.

29	  validateHistory as _validateHistory,
30	  validateOkrDocument as _validateOkrDocument,

48	// ── rendering Ajv errors ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
49	//
50	// Ajv reports the root as '' and nested paths as '/tree/nodes/0/id'. Render
51	// that as something a human can act on without leaking Ajv's shape.
52	
53	// Read a value out of `data` by Ajv instancePath ('' is the root).
54	function at(data, instancePath) {
55	  if (!instancePath) return data;
56	  let cur = data;
57	  for (const raw of instancePath.slice(1).split('/')) {
58	    if (cur == null) return undefined;
59	    cur = cur[raw.replace(/~1/g, '/').replace(/~0/g, '~')];
60	  }
61	  return cur;
62	}
63	
64	const quote = (v) => JSON.stringify(v);
65	
66	// Turn Ajv's error objects into "path: message" strings, optionally shifted
67	// under a prefix so a branch validated on its own still reports the path the
68	// caller sees (`/actions/0/fields`, not `/fields`).
69	function renderErrors(errors, prefix = '') {
70	  if (!errors?.length) return ['failed validation'];
71	
72	  // Merge allowed values per path: one enum failure per line, not per branch.
73	  const allowedByPath = new Map();
74	  for (const e of errors) {
75	    if (e.keyword !== 'enum' || !Array.isArray(e.params?.allowedValues)) continue;
76	    const set = allowedByPath.get(e.instancePath) ?? new Set();
77	    for (const v of e.params.allowedValues) set.add(v);
78	    allowedByPath.set(e.instancePath, set);
79	  }
80	
81	  const seen = new Set();
82	  const out = [];
83	  for (const e of errors) {
84	    const path = prefix + e.instancePath || '/';
85	    let text;
86	    if (e.keyword === 'oneOf') continue; // the branch errors already say what is wrong
87	    else if (e.keyword === 'enum') {
88	      text = `${path}: must be one of ${[...allowedByPath.get(e.instancePath)].map(quote).join(', ')}`;
89	    } else if (e.keyword === 'additionalProperties') {
90	      text = `${path}: unknown property "${e.params.additionalProperty}"`;
91	    } else {
92	      text = `${path}: ${e.message ?? 'is invalid'}`;
93	    }
94	    if (seen.has(text)) continue;
95	    seen.add(text);
96	    out.push(text);
97	  }
98	  return out.length ? out : [`${prefix || '/'}: failed validation`];
99	}
100	
101	// ── actions: oneOf, narrowed by hand ────────────────────────────────────────
102	
103	const ACTION_BRANCHES = {
104	  edit: _validateEditAction,
105	  relink: _validateRelinkAction,
106	  add: _validateAddAction,
107	  delete: _validateDeleteAction
108	};
109	const ACTION_OPS = Object.keys(ACTION_BRANCHES);
110	
111	// Ajv reports a failed oneOf as all four branches' complaints at once, and a
112	// resolved $ref rewrites schemaPath relative to the branch — so there is no way
113	// to tell from the errors which branch was meant. Read the `op` ourselves and
114	// validate only that branch.
115	function actionErrors(value, prefix) {
116	  const root = prefix || '/';
117	  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return [`${root}: must be an object`];
118	  if (!('op' in value)) return [`${root}: must have required property 'op'`];
119	  const branch = ACTION_BRANCHES[value.op];
120	  if (!branch) return [`${prefix}/op: must be one of ${ACTION_OPS.map(quote).join(', ')}`];
121	  if (branch(value)) return []; // the branch is happy; the oneOf must have matched more than one
122	  return renderErrors(branch.errors, prefix);
123	}
124	
125	// Replace every oneOf failure over an Action with that branch's own errors.
126	// Applies to a bare action and to actions nested in a chat response alike.
127	function refineActionErrors(errors, data) {
128	  const prefixes = errors.filter((e) => e.keyword === 'oneOf').map((e) => e.instancePath);
129	  if (!prefixes.length) return renderErrors(errors);
130	  const untouched = errors.filter((e) => !prefixes.some((p) => e.instancePath.startsWith(p)));
131	  const refined = prefixes.flatMap((p) => actionErrors(at(data, p), p));
132	  return [...(untouched.length ? renderErrors(untouched) : []), ...refined];
133	}

135	// ── structural validation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
136	
137	// The precompiled validators park failures on `.errors`, which is overwritten
138	// on the next call — so read it immediately.
139	function wrap(validator, { actions = false } = {}) {
140	  return (data) => {
141	    if (validator(data)) return { ok: true, value: data };
142	    const errors = validator.errors ?? [];
143	    return { ok: false, errors: actions ? refineActionErrors(errors, data) : renderErrors(errors) };
144	  };
145	}

147	/** @type {(data: unknown) => { ok: true, value: any } | { ok: false, errors: string[] }} */
148	export const validateOkrDocument = wrap(_validateOkrDocument, { actions: true });
149	export const validateOkrTree = wrap(_validateOkrTree);
150	export const validateOkrNode = wrap(_validateOkrNode);
151	export const validateCompany = wrap(_validateCompany);

153	export const validateAction = wrap(_validateAction, { actions: true });

155	export const validateChatResponse = wrap(_validateChatResponse, { actions: true });

157	// ── semantic validation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
158	
159	const LADDER = { company: 0, objective: 1, kr: 2 };
160	
161	/**
162	 * Relational checks JSON Schema cannot express. Assumes the tree is already
163	 * structurally valid; run a validate* first.
164	 *
165	 * Errors make the tree unusable. Warnings are style: the level ladder is only
166	 * a warning because validateResponse and apply.js both allow free relinking,
167	 * so a tree mid-edit can legitimately sit off-ladder.
168	 */
169	export function checkTreeSemantics(tree) {
170	  const errors = [];
171	  const warnings = [];
172	  const nodes = tree?.nodes;
173	  if (!Array.isArray(nodes)) return { errors: ['/nodes: must be an array'], warnings };
174	
175	  const byId = new Map();
176	  for (const [i, n] of nodes.entries()) {
177	    if (byId.has(n.id)) errors.push(`/nodes/${i}/id: duplicate node id "${n.id}"`);
178	    else byId.set(n.id, n);
179	  }
180	
181	  const roots = nodes.filter((n) => n.parent == null);
182	  if (!roots.length) errors.push('/nodes: no root node (exactly one node must have parent: null)');
183	  else if (roots.length > 1) {
184	    errors.push(`/nodes: ${roots.length} root nodes (${roots.map((n) => n.id).join(', ')}), expected exactly one`);
185	  }
186	  for (const r of roots) if (r.level !== 'company') warnings.push(`/nodes: root "${r.id}" has level "${r.level}", expected "company"`);
187	  for (const n of nodes) {
188	    if (n.parent == null && n.level === 'company') continue;
189	    if (n.level === 'company' && n.parent != null) warnings.push(`/nodes: "${n.id}" has level "company" but is not the root`);
190	  }
191	
192	  for (const [i, n] of nodes.entries()) {
193	    if (n.parent == null) continue;
194	    const parent = byId.get(n.parent);
195	    if (!parent) {
196	      errors.push(`/nodes/${i}/parent: "${n.id}" points at missing parent "${n.parent}"`);
197	      continue;
198	    }
199	    if (LADDER[n.level] !== LADDER[parent.level] + 1) {
200	      warnings.push(`/nodes/${i}/level: "${n.id}" (${n.level}) hangs off "${parent.id}" (${parent.level})`);
201	    }
202	  }
203	
204	  // Walk up from every node; anything that does not terminate at a root is in
205	  // or below a cycle. Report each cycle once, by its lowest-sorting member.
206	  const reported = new Set();
207	  for (const start of nodes) {
208	    const seen = new Set();
209	    let cur = start;
210	    while (cur && cur.parent != null) {
211	      if (seen.has(cur.id)) break;
212	      seen.add(cur.id);
213	      const next = byId.get(cur.parent);
214	      if (!next) break; // already reported as a missing parent
215	      if (seen.has(next.id)) {
216	        const cycle = [...seen].filter((id) => byId.has(id)).sort();
217	        const key = cycle.join(',');
218	        if (!reported.has(key)) {
219	          reported.add(key);
220	          errors.push(`/nodes: parent cycle through ${cycle.join(' -> ')}`);
221	        }
222	        break;
223	      }
224	      cur = next;
225	    }
226	  }
227	
228	  return { errors, warnings };
229	}
230	
231	// ── documents ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

233	/**
234	 * Stamp a tree (and optionally company/history) into an exportable document.
235	 * @returns {object} an OkrDocument at the current SCHEMA_VERSION
236	 */
237	export function createDocument({ tree, company, history, meta } = {}) {
238	  const doc = {
239	    schemaVersion: SCHEMA_VERSION,
240	    meta: {
241	      ...meta,
242	      exportedAt: meta?.exportedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),
243	      generator: meta?.generator ?? `@okr-viewer/schema ${PACKAGE_VERSION}`
244	    },
245	    tree
246	  };
247	  if (company !== undefined) doc.company = company;
248	  if (history !== undefined) doc.history = history;
249	  return doc;
250	}
251	
252	/**
253	 * Read a document written by createDocument: parse, version-check, migrate,
254	 * validate structurally, then check semantics.
255	 *
256	 * @param {string | object} input JSON text or an already-parsed object
257	 * @returns {{ ok: true, document: object, warnings: string[] }
258	 *         | { ok: false, errors: string[], warnings: string[] }}
259	 */
260	export function parseDocument(input) {
261	  let raw = input;
262	  if (typeof input === 'string') {
263	    try {
264	      raw = JSON.parse(input);
265	    } catch (err) {
266	      return { ok: false, errors: [`/: not valid JSON (${err.message})`], warnings: [] };
267	    }
268	  }
269	  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) {
270	    return { ok: false, errors: ['/: expected a JSON object'], warnings: [] };
271	  }
272	
273	  const version = raw.schemaVersion;
274	  if (!Number.isInteger(version) || version < 1) {
275	    return { ok: false, errors: ['/schemaVersion: must be an integer >= 1'], warnings: [] };
276	  }
277	  if (version > SCHEMA_VERSION) {
278	    return {
279	      ok: false,
280	      errors: [
281	        `/schemaVersion: this file is version ${version}, but this build only reads up to ${SCHEMA_VERSION}. Update the app.`
282	      ],
283	      warnings: []
284	    };
285	  }
286	
287	  let document = raw;
288	  if (version < SCHEMA_VERSION) {
289	    const migrated = migrate(document, version);
290	    if (!migrated.ok) return { ok: false, errors: migrated.errors, warnings: [] };
291	    document = migrated.document;
292	  }
293	
294	  const structural = validateOkrDocument(document);
295	  if (!structural.ok) return { ok: false, errors: structural.errors, warnings: [] };
296	
297	  const { errors, warnings } = checkTreeSemantics(document.tree);
298	  if (errors.length) return { ok: false, errors, warnings };
299	  return { ok: true, document, warnings };
300	}

1	// Builds schema/dist/ from schema/src/. Six steps, each loud on failure:
2	//
3	//   1. meta-validate every src/*.schema.json against draft-07
4	//   2. generate dist/types.d.ts with the json-schema-to-typescript fork
5	//   3. precompile Ajv validators into dist/validators.js (+ .d.ts)
6	//   4. copy the raw schemas into dist/json/
7	//   5. flatten chat-response into dist/json/tool/respond-input.json for Claude
8	//   6. tsc --noEmit over the generated types
9	//
10	// Run it as `npm run build:schema` from the repo root.
11

13	import { createRequire } from 'node:module';

18	import Ajv from 'ajv';

22	import $RefParser from '@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser';

27	const DIST = join(PKG, 'dist');
28	
29	const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(PKG, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
30	const step = (n, what) => console.log(`[schema] ${n}/6 ${what}`);
31	const fail = (msg) => {
32	  console.error(`[schema] BUILD FAILED: ${msg}`);
33	  process.exit(1);

36	// The named validators consumers get, and the schema each one compiles from.

38	//
39	// The four *Action entries compile a single oneOf branch each. Ajv reports a
40	// oneOf failure as every branch's complaints at once, with no way to tell which
41	// branch an error came from — resolving a $ref rewrites schemaPath relative to
42	// the target. Validating the branch the `op` names gives a usable message.
43	const VALIDATORS = {
44	  validateOkrDocument: 'okr-document.schema.json',
45	  validateOkrTree: 'okr-tree.schema.json',
46	  validateOkrNode: 'okr-node.schema.json',
47	  validateCompany: 'company.schema.json',
48	  validateHistory: 'history.schema.json',

52	  validateEditAction: 'action.schema.json#/definitions/editAction',
53	  validateRelinkAction: 'action.schema.json#/definitions/relinkAction',
54	  validateAddAction: 'action.schema.json#/definitions/addAction',
55	  validateDeleteAction: 'action.schema.json#/definitions/deleteAction'
56	};
57	
58	const BASE = 'https://okr-viewer.dev/schema/v1/';

60	rmSync(DIST, { recursive: true, force: true });

1	// applyAction(tree, action) → new tree.
2	//
3	// Pure: never mutates the input. Untouched node objects are reused by
4	// reference so the graph can diff by identity and keep its layout warm.
5	//
6	// The JSDoc types come from @okr-viewer/schema's generated declarations, so an
7	// editor checks this file against the same schema the service validates with,
8	// without either package adopting TypeScript.
9	
10	/**
11	 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').OkrTree} OkrTree
12	 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').OkrNode} OkrNode
13	 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').Action} Action
14	 */
15	
16	const EDITABLE = ['label', 'owner', 'metric', 'target', 'contributes', 'parent'];
17	
18	const clamp01 = (n) => (Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(1, Math.max(0, n)) : 0.5);
19	
20	function pick(fields = {}, extra = []) {
21	  const out = {};
22	  for (const k of [...EDITABLE, ...extra]) if (k in fields) out[k] = fields[k];
23	  if ('contributes' in out) out.contributes = clamp01(Number(out.contributes));
24	  return out;
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Every node below `id`, transitively.
29	 * @param {OkrTree} tree
30	 * @param {string} id
31	 * @returns {Set<string>}
32	 */
33	export function descendants(tree, id) {
34	  const out = new Set();
35	  let frontier = [id];
36	  while (frontier.length) {
37	    const next = tree.nodes.filter((n) => frontier.includes(n.parent)).map((n) => n.id);
38	    frontier = next.filter((x) => !out.has(x));
39	    frontier.forEach((x) => out.add(x));
40	  }
41	  return out;
42	}
43	
44	function wouldCycle(tree, id, newParent) {
45	  if (!newParent) return false;
46	  if (newParent === id) return true;
47	  return descendants(tree, id).has(newParent);
48	}
49	
50	/**
51	 * Apply one action, returning a new tree. Anything that does not fit the tree
52	 * (an unknown id, a parent that would make a cycle) is ignored rather than
53	 * thrown — the service has already filtered the model's output.
54	 * @param {OkrTree} tree
55	 * @param {Action} action
56	 * @returns {OkrTree}
57	 */
58	export function applyAction(tree, action) {
59	  if (!action || typeof action.id !== 'string') return tree;
60	  const { op, id } = action;
61	  const exists = tree.nodes.some((n) => n.id === id);
62	
63	  switch (op) {
64	    case 'edit':
65	    case 'relink': {
66	      if (!exists) return tree;
67	      const fields = pick(action.fields);
68	      if ('parent' in fields && wouldCycle(tree, id, fields.parent)) delete fields.parent;
69	      if (!Object.keys(fields).length) return tree;
70	      return { nodes: tree.nodes.map((n) => (n.id === id ? { ...n, ...fields } : n)) };
71	    }
72	
73	    case 'add': {
74	      if (exists) return applyAction(tree, { ...action, op: 'edit' });
75	      const node = {
76	        id,
77	        level: 'kr',
78	        parent: null,
79	        label: '(untitled)',
80	        owner: '',
81	        metric: '',
82	        target: '',
83	        contributes: 0.5,
84	        ...pick(action.fields, ['level'])
85	      };
86	      return { nodes: [...tree.nodes, node] };
87	    }
88	
89	    case 'delete': {
90	      if (!exists) return tree;
91	      const gone = descendants(tree, id);
92	      gone.add(id);
93	      return { nodes: tree.nodes.filter((n) => !gone.has(n.id)) };
94	    }
95	
96	    default:
97	      return tree;
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * @param {OkrTree} tree
103	 * @param {Action[]} actions
104	 * @returns {OkrTree}
105	 */
106	export function applyActions(tree, actions = []) {
107	  return actions.reduce(applyAction, tree);
108	}

6	  let { tree, selectedId = null, highlight = [], onSelect } = $props();

8	  let el;
9	  // The graph instance lives outside Svelte's reactive system on purpose:
10	  // 3d-force-graph mutates its own data and runs its own render loop.
11	  let graph;
12	  const meshes = new Map(); // node id → THREE.Mesh, for the pulse loop
13	  let highlightSet = new Set();
14	  let raf;
15	  const WORLD_UP = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
16	  // { from, to, start, ms } while a programmatic move is re-levelling camera.up.
17	  let upTween = null;
18	
19	  const LEVEL = {
20	    company: { color: '#f5c542', size: 10 },
21	    objective: { color: '#4f9cff', size: 6.5 },
22	    kr: { color: '#5ad38a', size: 3.6 }
23	  };
24	  const WHITE = new THREE.Color('#ffffff');
25	  const RED = new THREE.Color('#ff3b30');
26	
27	  // contributes 0 → red, 1 → green
28	  function linkColor(c) {
29	    const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, c ?? 0.5));
30	    return `hsl(${Math.round(120 * t)}, 75%, ${52 - 10 * t}%)`;
31	  }
32	
33	  const esc = (s) => String(s ?? '').replace(/[&<>"]/g, (ch) => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' })[ch]);
34	
35	  function makeNodeObject(node) {
36	    const cfg = LEVEL[node.level] ?? LEVEL.kr;
37	    const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(
38	      new THREE.SphereGeometry(cfg.size, 24, 24),
39	      new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({ color: cfg.color, transparent: true, opacity: 0.95 })
40	    );
41	    mesh.userData.baseColor = new THREE.Color(cfg.color);
42	    meshes.set(node.id, mesh);
43	    return mesh;
44	  }
45	
46	  // Reuse existing node objects (they carry x/y/z) so an edit nudges the
47	  // layout instead of re-heating the whole simulation.
48	  function toGraphData(t, prev) {
49	    const prevById = new Map((prev?.nodes ?? []).map((n) => [n.id, n]));
50	    const nodes = t.nodes.map((n) => {
51	      const existing = prevById.get(n.id);
52	      return existing ? Object.assign(existing, n) : { ...n };
53	    });
54	    const ids = new Set(nodes.map((n) => n.id));
55	    const links = t.nodes
56	      .filter((n) => n.parent && ids.has(n.parent))
57	      .map((n) => ({ source: n.parent, target: n.id, contributes: n.contributes ?? 0.5 }));

61	  // Trackball lets the user roll `camera.up` freely; every programmatic move

63	  function levelCamera(ms) {

65	    const cam = graph.camera();
66	    const controls = graph.controls();
67	    if (!cam || !controls) return;
68	    const from = cam.up.clone().normalize();
69	    const view = controls.target.clone().sub(cam.position).normalize();
70	    // Looking (almost) straight down the tree makes lookAt with up = +Y undefined.
71	    let to = WORLD_UP.clone();
72	    if (Math.abs(view.dot(WORLD_UP)) > 0.98) to = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, -1);
73	    if (from.distanceToSquared(to) < 1e-6) { upTween = null; return; }
74	    // Upside down: a straight lerp would pass through the origin, so nudge off the antipode.
75	    if (from.dot(to) < -0.999) {

83	  export function flyTo(ids, ms = 1200) {

87	    if (!nodes.length) return;
88	    levelCamera(ms);
89	    const c = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 };
90	    for (const n of nodes) { c.x += n.x; c.y += n.y; c.z += n.z; }
91	    c.x /= nodes.length; c.y /= nodes.length; c.z /= nodes.length;
92	    let radius = 0;
93	    for (const n of nodes) radius = Math.max(radius, Math.hypot(n.x - c.x, n.y - c.y, n.z - c.z));

36

24	## The tree

Levels: company (the single root) → objective (team-level) → kr (key result). \`contributes\` (0–1) is a hand-assessed score of how well a node supports its parent; anything below 0.4 is a misalignment worth calling out. A KR with an empty or vague \`metric\` or \`target\` is not measurable. A KR that describes an activity ("run an offsite", "attend events") rather than an outcome is weak even if it has a number.

1	// Claude will occasionally invent node IDs. Everything it sends back is
2	// filtered against the tree the browser sent us, so nothing unknown reaches
3	// the renderer.
4	//
5	// Two layers, and the split matters:
6	//
7	//   @okr-viewer/schema's validateAction()  — shape. Is this an action at all?
8	//   the checks below                       — reference. Does it fit *this* tree?
9	//
10	// Shape lives in the package because the browser needs the same answer. The
11	// referential checks are tree-relative and stay here.
12	
13	import { validateAction } from '@okr-viewer/schema';
14	
15	// Keep only well-formed turns, cap the length, and merge consecutive
16	// same-role turns so the API always sees strict user/assistant alternation.
17	export function sanitizeHistory(history, maxTurns = 12) {
18	  const turns = (Array.isArray(history) ? history : [])
19	    .filter((m) => m && (m.role === 'user' || m.role === 'assistant') && typeof m.content === 'string' && m.content.trim())
20	    .slice(-maxTurns)
21	    .map((m) => ({ role: m.role, content: m.content.trim() }));
22	  while (turns.length && turns[0].role !== 'user') turns.shift();
23	  return mergeTurns(turns);
24	}
25	
26	export function mergeTurns(turns) {
27	  const out = [];
28	  for (const t of turns) {
29	    const last = out[out.length - 1];
30	    if (last && last.role === t.role) last.content += '\n\n' + t.content;
31	    else out.push({ ...t });
32	  }
33	  return out;
34	}
35	
36	export function validateResponse(tree, input) {
37	  const known = new Set(tree.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
38	  const parentOf = new Map(tree.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n.parent]));
39	  const dropped = [];
40	  const actions = [];
41	
42	  const isAncestorOrSelf = (candidate, id) => {
43	    let cur = candidate;
44	    for (let i = 0; cur != null && i < 1000; i++) {
45	      if (cur === id) return true;
46	      cur = parentOf.get(cur) ?? null;
47	    }
48	    return false;
49	  };
50	
51	  const validParent = (id, parent) => parent != null && known.has(parent) && !isAncestorOrSelf(parent, id);
52	
53	  for (const a of Array.isArray(input?.actions) ? input.actions : []) {
54	    const reject = (reason) => dropped.push({ action: a, reason });
55	
56	    // Shape first: op, id and the per-op field whitelist all come from the
57	    // shared schema, so anything past here has the keys it claims to have.
58	    const shape = validateAction(a);
59	    if (!shape.ok) {
60	      reject(shape.errors.join('; '));
61	      continue;
62	    }
63	
64	    const { op, id } = a;
65	    const fields = { ...a.fields };
66	
67	    if (op === 'edit' || op === 'relink') {
68	      if (!known.has(id)) { reject(`unknown id ${id}`); continue; }
69	      if ('parent' in fields && !validParent(id, fields.parent)) {
70	        reject(`bad parent ${fields.parent} for ${id}`);
71	        delete fields.parent;
72	      }
73	      // A relink whose only field was the rejected parent has nothing left.
74	      if (!Object.keys(fields).length) { reject('no usable fields'); continue; }
75	      if ('parent' in fields) parentOf.set(id, fields.parent);
76	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
77	    } else if (op === 'add') {
78	      if (known.has(id)) { reject(`add with existing id ${id}`); continue; }
79	      // The model is never allowed to mint a second company root.
80	      if (!fields.level || fields.level === 'company') fields.level = 'kr';
81	      if (!(fields.parent != null && known.has(fields.parent))) { reject(`add with bad parent ${fields.parent}`); continue; }
82	      known.add(id);
83	      parentOf.set(id, fields.parent);
84	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
85	    } else if (op === 'delete') {
86	      if (!known.has(id)) { reject(`unknown id ${id}`); continue; }
87	      const gone = new Set([id]);
88	      let grew = true;
89	      while (grew) {
90	        grew = false;
91	        for (const [child, parent] of parentOf) {
92	          if (gone.has(parent) && !gone.has(child)) { gone.add(child); grew = true; }
93	        }
94	      }
95	      for (const g of gone) { known.delete(g); parentOf.delete(g); }
96	      actions.push({ op, id });
97	    }
98	  }
99	
100	  const highlight = [
101	    ...new Set((Array.isArray(input?.highlight) ? input.highlight : []).filter((id) => typeof id === 'string' && known.has(id)))
102	  ];
103	
104	  const reply =
105	    typeof input?.reply === 'string' && input.reply.trim()
106	      ? input.reply.trim()
107	      : actions.length
108	        ? 'Done.'
109	        : "I couldn't come up with an answer for that — try rephrasing.";
110	
111	  return { reply, actions, highlight, dropped };
112	}

11	import manifest from '../assets/datasets/manifest.json';
12	import { parseDocument } from '@okr-viewer/schema';
13	
14	const files = import.meta.glob('../assets/datasets/*.json', { eager: true, import: 'default' });
15	
16	const slugOf = (path) => path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1, -'.json'.length);
17	
18	const documents = new Map();
19	for (const [path, document] of Object.entries(files)) {
20	  const slug = slugOf(path);
21	  if (slug === 'manifest') continue;

23	}

26	// dropping a new file into the folder works without touching the manifest.
27	const ordered = [
28	  ...(manifest.order ?? []).filter((id) => documents.has(id)),
29	  ...[...documents.keys()].filter((id) => !(manifest.order ?? []).includes(id)).sort()
30	];
31	
32	/** @type {{ id: string, title: string, document: object }[]} */
33	export const DATASETS = ordered.map((id) => ({
34	  id,
35	  title: documents.get(id).meta?.title || id,
36	  document: documents.get(id)
37	}));

40	  // A blank page with a stack trace beats a silent fallback to whichever file
41	  // happened to sort first.

44	  );
45	}

48	export const DEFAULT_DATASET_ID = manifest.default;
49	
50	/** @returns {{ id: string, title: string, document: object }} the dataset, or the default if `id` is unknown. */
51	export function getDataset(id) {
52	  return DATASETS.find((d) => d.id === id) ?? DATASETS.find((d) => d.id === DEFAULT_DATASET_ID);

// Every fixture under test/fixtures/ is a self-describing case:
//
//   { "schema": "okr-tree", "data": … }            must validate
//   { "schema": "okr-tree", "at": "/nodes", "data": … }  must fail, with an
//                                                        error on that path
//
// Adding a case is adding a file. `at: ""` means "fail anywhere", for the
// whole-object failures (a missing required property reports on the parent).

import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

import {
  validateAction,
  validateChatRequest,
  validateChatResponse,
  validateCompany,
  validateHistory,
  validateOkrDocument,
  validateOkrNode,
  validateOkrTree
} from '../index.js';

const BY_NAME = {
  action: validateAction,
  'chat-request': validateChatRequest,
  'chat-response': validateChatResponse,
  company: validateCompany,
  history: validateHistory,
  'okr-document': validateOkrDocument,
  'okr-node': validateOkrNode,
  'okr-tree': validateOkrTree
};

const FIXTURES = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/', import.meta.url));
const load = (kind) =>
  readdirSync(join(FIXTURES, kind))
    .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
    .sort()
    .map((f) => [f, JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(FIXTURES, kind, f), 'utf8'))]);

test('every fixture names a schema this package validates', () => {
  for (const kind of ['valid', 'invalid']) {
    for (const [name, fx] of load(kind)) {
      assert.ok(BY_NAME[fx.schema], `${kind}/${name} names unknown schema "${fx.schema}"`);
    }
  }
});

test('valid fixtures validate', async (t) => {
  const fixtures = load('valid');
  assert.ok(fixtures.length >= 10, 'expected a meaningful number of valid fixtures');
  for (const [name, fx] of fixtures) {
    await t.test(name, () => {
      const out = BY_NAME[fx.schema](fx.data);
      assert.ok(out.ok, `expected ${name} to validate, got:\n  ${out.errors?.join('\n  ')}`);
    });
  }
});

test('invalid fixtures fail on the path they name', async (t) => {
  const fixtures = load('invalid');
  assert.ok(fixtures.length >= 10, 'expected a meaningful number of invalid fixtures');
  for (const [name, fx] of fixtures) {
    await t.test(name, () => {
      const out = BY_NAME[fx.schema](fx.data);
      assert.equal(out.ok, false, `expected ${name} to fail validation`);
      assert.ok(out.errors.length, 'a failure must come with at least one error');
      for (const e of out.errors) assert.match(e, /^\S*: /, `error is not "path: message": ${e}`);
      if (fx.at) {
        assert.ok(
          out.errors.some((e) => e.startsWith(`${fx.at}:`)),
          `expected an error on "${fx.at}", got:\n  ${out.errors.join('\n  ')}`
        );
      }
    });
  }
});

test('errors never leak raw Ajv objects', () => {
  const out = validateOkrTree({ nodes: [{ id: 1 }] });
  assert.equal(out.ok, false);
  for (const e of out.errors) assert.equal(typeof e, 'string');
});

// Guards on what scripts/build.mjs emits. These catch a regression in the
// generator or the fork that the build's own checks might not, and they fail
// loudly if someone runs the tests against a stale dist/.

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

import { RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA } from '../index.js';

const read = (p) => readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL(p, import.meta.url)), 'utf8');

test('each generated type is declared exactly once', () => {
  const types = read('../dist/types.d.ts');
  for (const name of ['OkrNode', 'OkrTree', 'OkrDocument', 'Company', 'History', 'ChatRequest', 'ChatResponse']) {
    const count = types.match(new RegExp(`^export interface ${name} \\{`, 'gm'))?.length ?? 0;
    assert.equal(count, 1, `expected exactly one "export interface ${name}", found ${count}`);
  }
});

test('no suffixed duplicate types — the whole reason for the json2ts fork', () => {
  const dupes = read('../dist/types.d.ts').match(/^export (?:interface|type) \w+?\d+\b/gm) ?? [];
  assert.deepEqual(dupes, [], 'upstream json-schema-to-typescript inlines annotated $refs and suffixes the copies');
});

test('Action is a discriminated union of the four ops', () => {
  const types = read('../dist/types.d.ts');
  assert.match(types, /export type Action = EditAction \| RelinkAction \| AddAction \| DeleteAction;/);
});

test('the tool schema is fully flattened', () => {
  const text = JSON.stringify(RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA);
  for (const key of ['$ref', '$id', '$schema', 'definitions']) {
    assert.equal(text.includes(`"${key}"`), false, `respond-input.json still contains "${key}"`);
  }
});

test('the tool schema is a usable Claude input_schema', () => {
  assert.equal(RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA.type, 'object');
  assert.deepEqual(RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA.required, ['reply', 'actions', 'highlight']);
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA.properties).sort(), ['actions', 'highlight', 'reply']);
});

test('every field the model can send carries a description written for it', () => {
  const walk = (node, path) => {
    if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return;
    if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach((v, i) => walk(v, `${path}/${i}`));
    for (const [name, prop] of Object.entries(node.properties ?? {})) {
      assert.ok(prop.description, `${path}/properties/${name} has no description`);
      walk(prop, `${path}/properties/${name}`);
    }
    for (const key of ['items', 'oneOf', 'anyOf', 'allOf']) if (node[key]) walk(node[key], `${path}/${key}`);
  };
  walk(RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA, '');
});

:root {
  --bg: #0b0f17;
  --panel: #121826;
  --panel-2: #182033;
  --border: #243049;
  --text: #e6ebf5;
  --muted: #8b96ad;
  --accent: #4f9cff;
  --company: #f5c542;
  --objective: #4f9cff;
  --kr: #5ad38a;
  --bad: #ff5a4e;
  --meh: #f5c542;
  --good: #5ad38a;
  color-scheme: dark;
}

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

html, body, #app { height: 100%; margin: 0; }

body {
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--text);
  font: 14px/1.45 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Inter, system-ui, sans-serif;
  overflow: hidden;
}

button {
  font: inherit;
  color: inherit;
  background: var(--panel-2);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 6px 12px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
button:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--accent); }
button:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }
button.ghost { background: transparent; }
button.link {
  background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; text-align: left;
  color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer;
}
button.link:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

/* ── layout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.app { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; }

.topbar {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 20px;
  padding: 10px 16px;
  background: var(--panel);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.topbar .brand { font-weight: 600; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
.topbar .dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--company); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--company); }
.topbar .stats { color: var(--muted); }
.topbar .stats .warn { color: var(--bad); }
.topbar .buttons { margin-left: auto; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
/* the dataset picker, dressed as button.ghost so the topbar stays one row of controls */
.topbar select {
  font: inherit;
  color: inherit;
  background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 6px 10px;
  cursor: pointer;
  max-width: 220px;
}
.topbar select:hover { border-color: var(--accent); }
.topbar select option { background: var(--panel-2); color: var(--text); }

main { flex: 1; display: flex; min-height: 0; }

.stage { position: relative; flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
.graph { position: absolute; inset: 0; }

.legend {
  position: absolute; right: 14px; bottom: 12px;
  display: flex; gap: 14px; flex-wrap: wrap;
  color: var(--muted); font-size: 12px;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.legend span { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; }
.legend .sw { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; }
.legend .sw.company { background: var(--company); }
.legend .sw.objective { background: var(--objective); }
.legend .sw.kr { background: var(--kr); }
.legend .sw.line { width: 22px; height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--bad), var(--good)); }

/* 3d-force-graph tooltip */
.scene-tooltip .tip { background: rgba(18, 24, 38, 0.95); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 10px; max-width: 280px; font-size: 13px; }
.scene-tooltip .tip span { display: block; color: var(--muted); font-size: 12px; margin-top: 2px; }

/* ── detail panel ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.detail {
  position: absolute; left: 14px; top: 14px;
  width: 320px; max-height: calc(100% - 28px); overflow: auto;
  background: rgba(18, 24, 38, 0.94);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 14px 16px;
  backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
}
.detail header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; }
.detail .level { font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-weight: 600; }
.detail .level.company { color: var(--company); }
.detail .level.objective { color: var(--objective); }
.detail .level.kr { color: var(--kr); }
.detail .close { background: none; border: 0; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1; padding: 0 4px; color: var(--muted); }
.detail h2 { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0 12px; line-height: 1.3; }
.detail h3 { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); margin: 14px 0 6px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; }
.detail dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 64px 1fr; gap: 6px 10px; margin: 0; }
.detail dt { color: var(--muted); }
.detail dd { margin: 0; }
.detail dd.empty { color: var(--bad); font-style: italic; }
.detail .fit { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
.detail .bar { flex: 1; height: 6px; background: var(--panel-2); border-radius: 3px; overflow: hidden; }
.detail .bar span { display: block; height: 100%; }
.detail ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }
.detail li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; align-items: baseline; }
.detail .id { color: var(--muted); font-size: 11px; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; margin: 12px 0 0; }

/* ── detail panel, edit mode ────────────────────────────────────────── */
.detail .tools { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; }
.detail .edit-toggle {
  font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-weight: 600;
  padding: 3px 10px; border-radius: 999px;
  background: transparent; color: var(--muted);
}
.detail .edit-toggle:hover { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--text); }
.detail .edit-toggle.on { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
/* inputs dressed like the chat composer, so the panel stays one surface */
.detail input:not([type="range"]),
.detail textarea,
.detail select {
  width: 100%; font: inherit; color: inherit;
  background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 4px 8px;
}
.detail input:focus, .detail textarea:focus, .detail select:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent); }
.detail textarea.label-input { resize: vertical; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.3; margin: 8px 0 12px; }
.detail .invalid, .detail .invalid:focus { border-color: var(--bad); outline: 1px solid var(--bad); }
.detail input.range { flex: 1; width: auto; accent-color: var(--accent); padding: 0; }
.detail select option { background: var(--panel-2); color: var(--text); }
.detail .actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin-top: 14px; }
.detail .actions button { font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 10px; }
.detail .actions .danger { color: var(--bad); }
.detail .actions .danger:hover { border-color: var(--bad); }
.bar .good, .pct.good { background: var(--good); }
.bar .meh, .pct.meh { background: var(--meh); }
.bar .bad, .pct.bad { background: var(--bad); }
.pct { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: #0b0f17; border-radius: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; white-space: nowrap; }

/* ── chat ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.chat {
  width: 380px; flex: none;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  background: var(--panel);
  border-left: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.messages { flex: 1; overflow: auto; padding: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
.empty { color: var(--muted); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; margin-top: auto; }
.empty p { margin: 0 0 4px; }
.chip { text-align: left; border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; background: var(--panel-2); color: var(--text); }
.msg { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; max-width: 92%; }
.msg.user { align-self: flex-end; align-items: flex-end; }
.msg.assistant { align-self: flex-start; }
.bubble { padding: 9px 12px; border-radius: 12px; white-space: pre-wrap; background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); }
.msg.user .bubble { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }
.msg.error .bubble { border-color: var(--bad); color: var(--bad); }
.msg.note .bubble { color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; background: transparent; }
.meta { display: flex; gap: 6px; }
.pill { font-size: 11px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--muted); }
.pill.edit { border-color: var(--good); color: var(--good); }
.thinking { display: flex; gap: 4px; padding: 12px 14px; }
.thinking span { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted); animation: blink 1.2s infinite; }
.thinking span:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.2s; }
.thinking span:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.4s; }
@keyframes blink { 0%, 80%, 100% { opacity: 0.25; } 40% { opacity: 1; } }

.chat form { display: flex; gap: 8px; padding: 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.chat textarea {
  flex: 1; resize: none; font: inherit; color: inherit;
  background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 10px;
}
.chat textarea:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent); }
.chat form button { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }

/**
 * The same relational checks, over the org rather than the tree: unique unit
 * ids, parents that exist, no parent cycles, a `lead` that names a real person,
 * a person in a real unit.
 *
 * `charter.dependsOn` pointing at a unit that is not there is a warning, not an
 * error: deleting a team leaves every charter that depended on it dangling, and
 * that should not make the document unreadable.
 *
 * @param {unknown} company
 * @returns {{ errors: string[], warnings: string[] }}
 */
export function checkCompanySemantics(company) {
  const errors = [];
  const warnings = [];
  const units = company?.units;
  if (!Array.isArray(units)) return { errors: ['/units: must be an array'], warnings };

  const byId = new Map();
  for (const [i, u] of units.entries()) {
    if (byId.has(u.id)) errors.push(`/units/${i}/id: duplicate unit id "${u.id}"`);
    else byId.set(u.id, u);
  }

  const people = Array.isArray(company?.people) ? company.people : [];
  const peopleById = new Map();
  for (const [i, p] of people.entries()) {
    if (peopleById.has(p.id)) errors.push(`/people/${i}/id: duplicate person id "${p.id}"`);
    else peopleById.set(p.id, p);
  }

  for (const [i, u] of units.entries()) {
    if (u.parent != null && !byId.has(u.parent)) {
      errors.push(`/units/${i}/parent: "${u.id}" points at missing parent "${u.parent}"`);
    }
    if (u.lead != null && !peopleById.has(u.lead)) {
      errors.push(`/units/${i}/lead: "${u.id}" names missing person "${u.lead}"`);
    }
    for (const [j, dep] of (u.charter?.dependsOn ?? []).entries()) {
      if (!byId.has(dep)) warnings.push(`/units/${i}/charter/dependsOn/${j}: "${u.id}" depends on missing team "${dep}"`);
    }
  }

  for (const [i, p] of people.entries()) {
    if (!byId.has(p.unitId)) errors.push(`/people/${i}/unitId: "${p.id}" is in missing unit "${p.unitId}"`);
  }

  // Same walk as the tree: anything that does not terminate at a top-level unit
  // is in or below a cycle. Report each cycle once, by its lowest-sorting member.
  const reported = new Set();
  for (const start of units) {
    const seen = new Set();
    let cur = start;
    while (cur && cur.parent != null) {
      if (seen.has(cur.id)) break;
      seen.add(cur.id);
      const next = byId.get(cur.parent);
      if (!next) break; // already reported as a missing parent
      if (seen.has(next.id)) {
        const cycle = [...seen].filter((id) => byId.has(id)).sort();
        const key = cycle.join(',');
        if (!reported.has(key)) {
          reported.add(key);
          errors.push(`/units: parent cycle through ${cycle.join(' -> ')}`);
        }
        break;
      }
      cur = next;
    }
  }

  return { errors, warnings };
}

/**
 * Do the tree's `unitId` pointers land on teams that exist? Warnings only,
 * never errors: a tree mid-edit can legitimately dangle (a team was deleted,
 * or the document simply has no `company`), and a dangling unitId costs nothing
 * more than a node rendering its `owner` text instead of a team link.
 *
 * @param {unknown} tree
 * @param {unknown} company
 * @returns {{ errors: string[], warnings: string[] }}
 */
export function checkOwnership(tree, company) {
  const warnings = [];
  const nodes = tree?.nodes;
  if (!Array.isArray(nodes)) return { errors: [], warnings };
  const known = new Set((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => u.id));
  for (const [i, n] of nodes.entries()) {
    if (n.unitId == null) continue;
    if (!known.has(n.unitId)) warnings.push(`/nodes/${i}/unitId: "${n.id}" is owned by missing team "${n.unitId}"`);
  }
  return { errors: [], warnings };
}

});

// applyUnitAction(company, action) → new company.
//
// The org half of apply.js, and pure in exactly the same way: never mutates the
// input, returns the same object when an action does not apply, and reuses
// untouched unit objects by reference.
//
// Teams live in `company.units`, flat with parent pointers, in the same style
// as the tree — so the rules here read like apply.js on purpose: an unknown id
// is ignored, a parent that would make a cycle is dropped rather than thrown.

/**
 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').Company} Company
 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').CompanyUnit} CompanyUnit
 * @typedef {import('@okr-viewer/schema').Action} Action
 */

const CHARTER_KEYS = ['mission', 'process', 'owns', 'dependsOn'];

/** An empty org, for a document that arrived without one. */
export const emptyCompany = (name = 'Untitled') => ({ name, units: [] });

const unitsOf = (company) => (Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []);

/**
 * Display name of a team, or null when the id names nothing (a deleted team, a
 * document with no `company`). Callers fall back to the node's `owner` text.
 * @param {Company | null | undefined} company
 * @param {string | null | undefined} id
 * @returns {string | null}
 */
export function unitName(company, id) {
  if (!id) return null;
  return unitsOf(company).find((u) => u.id === id)?.name ?? null;
}

/**
 * Every team below `id`, transitively.
 * @param {Company | null | undefined} company
 * @param {string} id
 * @returns {Set<string>}
 */
export function unitDescendants(company, id) {
  const units = unitsOf(company);
  const out = new Set();
  let frontier = [id];
  while (frontier.length) {
    const next = units.filter((u) => frontier.includes(u.parent)).map((u) => u.id);
    frontier = next.filter((x) => !out.has(x));
    frontier.forEach((x) => out.add(x));
  }
  return out;
}

function wouldCycle(company, id, newParent) {
  if (!newParent) return false;
  if (newParent === id) return true;
  return unitDescendants(company, id).has(newParent);
}

// A charter edit is a shallow merge, one field at a time: the model that knows
// only the mission must not be able to blank out the process by omission.
function mergeCharter(existing, patch) {
  const out = { ...existing };
  for (const k of CHARTER_KEYS) if (k in patch) out[k] = patch[k];
  // An empty charter is noise in the document; drop it rather than store `{}`.
  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : undefined;
}

function pickUnitFields(company, id, fields = {}) {
  const out = {};
  if (typeof fields.name === 'string' && fields.name.trim()) out.name = fields.name.trim();
  if ('parent' in fields && !wouldCycle(company, id, fields.parent)) out.parent = fields.parent ?? null;
  if (typeof fields.lead === 'string') out.lead = fields.lead;
  return out;
}

/**
 * Apply one unit action, returning a new company. Node ops are not this
 * function's business — applyDocumentActions routes them.
 *
 * `deleteUnit` never cascades: teams under the one being removed move up to its
 * parent. Deleting "Marketing" must not silently take Content and Field
 * Marketing with it, the way deleting a node takes its subtree.
 *
 * @param {Company} company
 * @param {Action} action
 * @returns {Company}
 */
export function applyUnitAction(company, action) {
  if (!company || !action || typeof action.id !== 'string') return company;
  const { op, id } = action;
  const units = unitsOf(company);
  const existing = units.find((u) => u.id === id) ?? null;

  switch (op) {
    case 'editUnit': {
      if (!existing) return company;
      const fields = pickUnitFields(company, id, action.fields);
      const charter =
        action.fields && 'charter' in action.fields ? mergeCharter(existing.charter, action.fields.charter ?? {}) : undefined;
      if (!Object.keys(fields).length && charter === undefined) return company;
      const next = { ...existing, ...fields };
      if (charter !== undefined) next.charter = charter;
      else if (action.fields && 'charter' in action.fields) delete next.charter;
      return { ...company, units: units.map((u) => (u.id === id ? next : u)) };
    }

    case 'addUnit': {
      if (existing) return applyUnitAction(company, { ...action, op: 'editUnit' });
      const fields = action.fields ?? {};
      const unit = { id, name: String(fields.name ?? 'New team').trim() || 'New team', parent: fields.parent ?? null };
      if (unit.parent != null && !units.some((u) => u.id === unit.parent)) unit.parent = null;
      const charter = mergeCharter(undefined, fields.charter ?? {});
      if (charter) unit.charter = charter;
      return { ...company, units: [...units, unit] };
    }

    case 'deleteUnit': {
      if (!existing) return company;
      const up = existing.parent ?? null;
      const next = units
        .filter((u) => u.id !== id)
        .map((u) => {
          // Children move up; anyone who depended on the team stops depending
          // on a ghost.
          const reparented = u.parent === id ? { ...u, parent: up } : u;
          const deps = reparented.charter?.dependsOn;
          if (!deps?.includes(id)) return reparented;
          const kept = deps.filter((d) => d !== id);
          const charter = { ...reparented.charter };
          if (kept.length) charter.dependsOn = kept;
          else delete charter.dependsOn;
          return { ...reparented, charter: Object.keys(charter).length ? charter : undefined };
        })
        .map((u) => (u.charter === undefined && 'charter' in u ? (({ charter, ...rest }) => rest)(u) : u));
      return { ...company, units: next };
    }

    default:
      return company;
  }
}

/**
 * The document-level apply: node ops go to applyAction, team ops to
 * applyUnitAction, and the two are joined here.
 *
 * Two joins, both of them the invariant "owner never disagrees with unitId"
 * (Concepts/Teams as Agents):
 *
 *   - a node op that sets `unitId` without saying `owner` gets `owner` filled
 *     in from the team's name, so a prompt that reads `owner` and a prompt that
 *     reads `unitId` agree;
 *   - `deleteUnit` clears that `unitId` off every node it owned, keeping the
 *     `owner` text so the node still says who is accountable.
 *
 * @param {{ tree: OkrTree, company: Company | null }} document
 * @param {Action[]} actions
 * @returns {{ tree: OkrTree, company: Company | null }}
 */
export function applyDocumentActions({ tree, company = null }, actions = []) {
  let nextTree = tree;
  let nextCompany = company;

  for (const action of actions) {
    if (UNIT_OPS.has(action?.op)) {
      nextCompany = applyUnitAction(nextCompany, action);
      if (action.op === 'deleteUnit') {
        const orphaned = nextTree.nodes.some((n) => n.unitId === action.id);
        if (orphaned) {
          nextTree = { nodes: nextTree.nodes.map((n) => (n.unitId === action.id ? { ...n, unitId: null } : n)) };
        }
      }
      continue;
    }

    let resolved = action;
    const fields = action?.fields;
    if (fields && 'unitId' in fields && !('owner' in fields)) {
      // null unitId means "no team"; the owner text it leaves behind is the
      // last thing the user saw, so only a real team overwrites it.
      const name = unitName(nextCompany, fields.unitId);
      if (name != null) resolved = { ...action, fields: { ...fields, owner: name } };
    }
    nextTree = applyAction(nextTree, resolved);
  }

  return { tree: nextTree, company: nextCompany };
}

/**
 * Tree-only apply, kept for callers (and tests) that have no org in hand.
 * @param {OkrTree} tree
 * @param {Action[]} actions
 * @returns {OkrTree}
 */
export function applyActions(tree, actions = []) {
  return applyDocumentActions({ tree, company: null }, actions).tree;
}

def build(file, parents, charters, unit_name_fix=None):
    path = DIR + file
    doc = json.load(open(path))
    owners = []
    for n in doc['tree']['nodes']:
        o = n.get('owner', '')
        if o and o not in owners:
            owners.append(o)
    # every owner must be in the parent map
    missing = [o for o in owners if o not in parents]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f'{file}: no parent mapping for {missing}')
    # units in map order so parents come before children
    units = []
    for name, parent in parents.items():
        u = {'id': slug(name), 'name': name, 'parent': parent}
        if slug(name) in charters:
            u['charter'] = charters[slug(name)]
        units.append(u)
    company = {'name': doc['meta']['title'].split(',')[0], 'units': units}

    # rebuild the document with company after meta, and unitId after owner
    nodes = []
    for n in doc['tree']['nodes']:
        out = {}
        for k, v in n.items():
            out[k] = v
            if k == 'owner':
                out['unitId'] = slug(v) if v else None
        if 'unitId' not in out:
            out['unitId'] = None
        nodes.append(out)

    newdoc = {}
    for k, v in doc.items():
        if k == 'tree':
            newdoc['company'] = company
            newdoc['tree'] = {'nodes': nodes}
        else:
            newdoc[k] = v
    open(path, 'w').write(json.dumps(newdoc, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(f'{file}: {len(units)} units, {len(nodes)} nodes, {len(charters)} charters')


build('workflow-platform-fy26.json', WORKFLOW_PARENTS, WORKFLOW_CHARTERS)
build('starter.json', STARTER_PARENTS, STARTER_CHARTERS)
build('regional-clinic-network.json', CLINIC_PARENTS, CLINIC_CHARTERS)

"""// Ownership is the join between the two halves of a document, and it is the
// one a hand edit breaks silently: rename a unit id and every node that pointed
// at it renders its stale owner text instead. parseDocument warns about that,
// and the zero-warnings assertion above already covers it — this says so out
// loud, and adds the stricter bar a bundled dataset is held to: if it ships a
// company at all, every node names a team in it.
for (const file of FILES) {
  test(`${file} assigns every node to a team that exists`, () => {
    const doc = read(file);
    if (!doc.company) return; // a dataset without an org is legal; owner stays text
    const known = new Set(doc.company.units.map((u) => u.id));
    const dangling = doc.tree.nodes.filter((n) => n.unitId && !known.has(n.unitId)).map((n) => n.id);
    assert.deepEqual(dangling, [], `${file}: nodes pointing at missing teams: ${dangling.join(', ')}`);

    assert.deepEqual(unassigned, [], `${file}: nodes with no team: ${unassigned.join(', ')}`);
  });
}

<script>
  let { company, tree, onOpen, onAdd, onClose } = $props();

  // The org as an indented tree, same shape as the OKR tree: flat units with
  // parent pointers, walked depth-first. Units whose parent is missing are
  // shown at the top rather than hidden — a dangling parent should be visible,
  // not silently swallowed.
  const rows = $derived.by(() => {
    const units = company.units ?? [];
    const byParent = new Map();
    const ids = new Set(units.map((u) => u.id));
    for (const u of units) {
      const key = u.parent != null && ids.has(u.parent) ? u.parent : null;
      byParent.set(key, [...(byParent.get(key) ?? []), u]);
    }
    const out = [];
    const walk = (parent, depth) => {
      for (const u of byParent.get(parent) ?? []) {
        out.push({ unit: u, depth, owned: tree.nodes.filter((n) => n.unitId === u.id).length });
        walk(u.id, depth + 1);
      }
    };
    walk(null, 0);
    return out;
  });

  const unassigned = $derived(tree.nodes.filter((n) => n.unitId == null).length);
</script>

<aside class="detail teams">
  <header>
    <span class="level team">Teams</span>
    <div class="tools">
      <button class="close" onclick={onClose} aria-label="Close">×</button>
    </div>
  </header>

  <h2>{company.name}</h2>

  {#if rows.length}
    <ul class="tree">
      {#each rows as row (row.unit.id)}
        <li style="padding-left: {row.depth * 14}px">
          <button class="link" onclick={() => onOpen(row.unit.id)}>{row.unit.name}</button>
          <span class="count" class:none={!row.owned} title="{row.owned} node{row.owned === 1 ? '' : 's'} owned">
            {row.owned}
          </span>
        </li>
      {/each}
    </ul>
  {:else}
    <p class="hint">No teams yet. Add one and give it a charter — the assistant reads it.</p>
  {/if}

  {#if unassigned}
    <p class="hint">{unassigned} node{unassigned === 1 ? ' has' : 's have'} no team.</p>
  {/if}

  <div class="actions">
    <button class="ghost" onclick={onAdd}>+ Add team</button>
  </div>
</aside>

<script>
  import { unitDescendants } from './lib/company.js';

  let { unit, company, tree, onEdit, onSelect, onBack, onClose, onFocusField = () => {} } = $props();

  // A team panel is an editor: there is no read mode to toggle into, because a
  // charter is a thing you write, not a thing you look up. Same discipline as
  // Detail's edit mode though — `unit` stays the committed truth and `draft` is
  // only what the inputs hold between keystroke and commit, so an undo or an
  // assistant edit re-seeds the fields underneath the cursor.

  let draft = $state({ name: '', mission: '', process: '', owns: '' });
  let invalidName = $state(false);
  // What we last sent per field, because blur fires before the new `unit`
  // arrives and would otherwise re-send the edit Enter just committed.
  let sent = {};

  const ownsText = (u) => (u.charter?.owns ?? []).join('\n');

  // Keyed on the unit object: applyUnitAction hands back a new one for every
  // change, so a commit or an undo re-seeds the inputs.
  $effect(() => {
    const u = unit;
    draft = {
      name: u.name ?? '',
      mission: u.charter?.mission ?? '',
      process: u.charter?.process ?? '',
      owns: ownsText(u)
    };
    invalidName = false;
    sent = {};
  });

  const edit = (fields) => onEdit({ op: 'editUnit', id: unit.id, fields });

  function commitName() {
    const value = String(draft.name ?? '').trim();
    if (!value) {
      // schema: minLength 1. Put the old name back and mark the field; the mark
      // clears on the next keystroke, not on the blur that follows here.
      invalidName = true;
      draft.name = unit.name ?? '';
      return;
    }
    draft.name = value;
    if (value === unit.name || value === sent.name) return;
    sent.name = value;
    edit({ name: value });
  }

  // mission and process are prose, so Enter inserts a newline and blur commits.
  function commitProse(field) {
    const value = String(draft[field] ?? '').trim();
    draft[field] = value;
    if (value === (unit.charter?.[field] ?? '') || value === sent[field]) return;
    sent[field] = value;
    // An emptied field is sent as '' rather than dropped: the merge in
    // applyUnitAction is per-key, so '' is how you clear one.
    edit({ charter: { [field]: value } });
  }

  // One item per line in, an array out — a list because two teams claiming the
  // same thing is the point of `owns`.
  function commitOwns() {
    const items = String(draft.owns ?? '')
      .split('\n')
      .map((s) => s.trim())
      .filter(Boolean)
      .slice(0, 50) // schema: maxItems 50
      .map((s) => s.slice(0, 200)); // schema: maxLength 200
    const text = items.join('\n');
    draft.owns = text;
    if (text === ownsText(unit) || text === sent.owns) return;
    sent.owns = text;
    edit({ charter: { owns: items } });
  }

  function onProseKey(e, field, commit) {
    if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
    e.preventDefault();
    draft[field] = field === 'owns' ? ownsText(unit) : unit.charter?.[field] ?? '';
    e.currentTarget.blur();
  }

  function onNameKey(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      e.preventDefault();
      draft.name = unit.name ?? '';
      invalidName = false;
      e.currentTarget.blur();
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      e.preventDefault();
      commitName();
      e.currentTarget.blur();
    }
  }

  // ── org position and dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────

  const others = $derived.by(() => {
    const below = unitDescendants(company, unit.id);
    return company.units.filter((u) => u.id !== unit.id && !below.has(u.id));
  });

  function commitParent(e) {
    const value = e.currentTarget.value;
    const parent = value === '' ? null : value;
    if (parent === (unit.parent ?? null)) return;
    edit({ parent });
  }

  const dependsOn = $derived(unit.charter?.dependsOn ?? []);

  function toggleDependency(id, on) {
    const next = on ? [...dependsOn, id] : dependsOn.filter((d) => d !== id);
    edit({ charter: { dependsOn: next } });
  }

  // ── the nodes this team owns ──────────────────────────────────────────────

  const owned = $derived(tree.nodes.filter((n) => n.unitId === unit.id));

  function removeUnit() {
    const what = owned.length
      ? `Delete the ${unit.name} team? Its ${owned.length} node${owned.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} stay in the tree and lose their team.`
      : `Delete the ${unit.name} team?`;
    if (!confirm(what)) return;
    onEdit({ op: 'deleteUnit', id: unit.id });
    onBack();
  }
</script>

<aside class="detail teams editing">
  <header>
    <button class="link back" onclick={onBack}>← Teams</button>
    <div class="tools">
      <button class="close" onclick={onClose} aria-label="Close">×</button>
    </div>
  </header>

  <input
    class="label-input"
    class:invalid={invalidName}
    bind:value={draft.name}
    oninput={() => (invalidName = false)}
    onfocus={() => onFocusField('name')}
    onblur={() => commitName()}
    onkeydown={onNameKey}
    aria-label="Team name"
  />

  <dl>
    <dt>Part of</dt>
    <dd>
      <select value={unit.parent ?? ''} onchange={commitParent} aria-label="Part of">
        <option value="">— top of the org —</option>
        {#each others as choice (choice.id)}
          <option value={choice.id}>{choice.name}</option>
        {/each}
      </select>
    </dd>
  </dl>

  <h3>Mission</h3>
  <textarea
    rows="3"
    placeholder="Why this team exists, in its own words"
    bind:value={draft.mission}
    onfocus={() => onFocusField('charter.mission')}
    onblur={() => commitProse('mission')}
    onkeydown={(e) => onProseKey(e, 'mission')}
    aria-label="Mission"
  ></textarea>

  <h3>Process</h3>
  <textarea
    rows="4"
    placeholder="The process it runs: inputs, steps, outputs, cadence"
    bind:value={draft.process}
    onfocus={() => onFocusField('charter.process')}
    onblur={() => commitProse('process')}
    onkeydown={(e) => onProseKey(e, 'process')}
    aria-label="Process"
  ></textarea>

  <h3>Owns</h3>
  <textarea
    rows="4"
    placeholder="One system, metric or decision per line"
    bind:value={draft.owns}
    onfocus={() => onFocusField('charter.owns')}
    onblur={commitOwns}
    onkeydown={(e) => onProseKey(e, 'owns')}
    aria-label="Owns"
  ></textarea>

  {#if others.length}
    <h3>Depends on</h3>
    <ul class="checks">
      {#each others as other (other.id)}
        <li>
          <label>
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              checked={dependsOn.includes(other.id)}
              onchange={(e) => toggleDependency(other.id, e.currentTarget.checked)}
            />
            {other.name}
          </label>
        </li>
      {/each}
    </ul>
  {/if}

  <h3>{owned.length} node{owned.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} owned</h3>
  {#if owned.length}
    <ul>
      {#each owned as n (n.id)}
        <li><button class="link" onclick={() => onSelect(n.id)}>{n.label}</button></li>
      {/each}
    </ul>
  {:else}
    <p class="hint">Nothing in the tree points at this team yet.</p>
  {/if}

  <div class="actions">
    <button class="ghost danger" onclick={removeUnit}>Delete team</button>
  </div>

  <p class="id">{unit.id}</p>
</aside>
